primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: A pathogenic TTR variant destabilizes the native transthyretin tetramer. Tetramers dissociate more readily into pro-amyloidogenic monomers, which misassemble and polymerize into extracellular amyloid fibrils in peripheral nerves, heart, and other tissues.
vignette: A 48-year-old man has progressive burning pain and numbness in both feet, orthostatic lightheadedness, and alternating constipation and diarrhea. Echocardiography shows increased ventricular wall thickness with impaired diastolic filling. His father and paternal aunt developed similar neurologic and cardiac disease. Tissue biopsy shows Congo red-positive deposits, and genetic testing identifies a heterozygous pathogenic TTR variant.
lead: Which molecular event most directly promotes formation of the deposited fibrils in this patient?
correct: Destabilization and dissociation of transthyretin tetramers into pro-amyloidogenic monomers
distractors: Clonal production of misfolded immunoglobulin light chains by plasma cells
Persistent production of serum amyloid A during chronic inflammation
Retention and accumulation of beta-2 microglobulin during long-term hemodialysis
Proteolytic generation and aggregation of amyloid-beta peptides from amyloid precursor protein
distractor_notes: Misfolded immunoglobulin light chains produced by a plasma-cell clone cause AL amyloidosis. The identified TTR pathogenic variant and autosomal-dominant multisystem phenotype instead indicate ATTRv amyloidosis.
Serum amyloid A is the precursor in AA amyloidosis associated with sustained inflammatory states, not TTR variant amyloidosis.
Beta-2 microglobulin accumulation is associated with dialysis-related amyloidosis in long-term hemodialysis, which is not the inherited TTR mechanism in this patient.
Amyloid-beta is generated from amyloid precursor protein in Alzheimer disease and produces primarily CNS-localized amyloid rather than hereditary TTR systemic amyloidosis.
key_expl: Hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis can cause peripheral and autonomic neuropathy together with restrictive cardiomyopathy and is inherited in an autosomal-dominant pattern. TTR normally circulates as a tetramer. Disease-causing TTR variants reduce tetramer stability, allowing dissociation into pro-amyloidogenic monomers that polymerize into amyloid fibrils and deposit in tissues.
objective: Recognize ATTRv amyloidosis from its inherited neuropathic/cardiac phenotype and connect TTR pathogenic variants to tetramer destabilization, monomer formation, and amyloid fibril deposition.
